editorial.headline: Industrial Gas Manufacturing with a Clear National PMA Lane
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 20112 covers the making of core industrial gases, and the record marks it as nationally open to foreign-owned registration across all listed business scales.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20112 is the industrial-gas manufacturing activity: the making of basic chemicals that produce gases used across industrial systems. The record names hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, carbon dioxide, dry ice, and noble gases such as helium, neon, and argon. In plain English, this is not a trading or distribution classification; it is a production classification for the manufacture of industrial gases as basic chemical outputs.

That scope matters because the business profile implied by the record is broad in scale. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, so the classification is not reserved only for large plants in the national dataset. A small specialist producer and a larger industrial facility sit inside the same registered activity when the real work is manufacturing these gases. The editorial point is simple: the code is about what is being made, not the size of the company doing it.

Nationally, the foreign-investment signal is clean. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign ownership ceiling is 100%, with the cited source listed as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That means the slim record does not contain a national foreign-share cap below full ownership. There is no basis here to invent extra capital thresholds, special licences, or operating timelines; the record gives only the openness status, the ceiling, the source, and the business scales.

Bali does not change that into a local blockage on this record. For Bali, the record assigns the status OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and sets l4_bali_blocked to false. The reason is stated directly: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The moratorium rule in the record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent, but this activity is not marked as blocked under that rule. So the honest national-vs-Bali reading is not a warning dressed up as opportunity: nationally it is open, and for Bali the record does not mark it as blocked.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is that KBLI 20112 is nationally open to PMA and, on this record, not blocked for Bali registration.
